userStories.title: Read PR details from GitHub and GitLab
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Map GitHub and GitLab PR metadata to PrInfo with fail-closed repository identity.

**Motivation** — The forge layer can open, view, edit and promote a PR, and post one top-level comment (`packages/nax/src/workflow/promote.ts`). It cannot read review threads or comments, post on a line, reply in a thread, resolve a thread, or tell a fork PR from a trusted one.

**Approach** — `readPrInfo(ref: PrRef, deps, cwd): Promise<PrInfo>`
- GitHub: `gh api --hostname <host> repos/<repo>/pulls/<number>`. Maps `title`, `body ?? ""`, `html_url`, `draft`, `user.login`, `user.id`, `base.ref`, `head.ref`, `head.sha`. `state` is `merged` when `merged_at` is non-null, else `state`. `crossRepo` is false only when `head.repo.full_name` and `base.repo.full_name` are both non-empty strings and equal; anything else (a deleted fork has `head.repo: null`, a missing field) is true.
- GitLab: `glab api --hostname <host> projects/<encodeURIComponent(repo)>/merge_requests/<number>`. Maps `title`, `description ?? ""`, `web_url`, `draft`, `author.username`, `author.id`, `target_branch`, `source_branch`, `sha`, `diff_refs.{base_sha,start_sha,head_sha}`. `state`: `opened` -> open, `merged` -> merged, anything else -> closed. `crossRepo` is false only when `source_project_id` and `target_project_id` are both numbers and equal; anything else is true (fail closed).
- A non-zero exit throws `NaxError` `FORGE_PR_READ_FAILED`; stdout that does not parse, or lacks `head.sha` / `sha`, throws `FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE`.

Every `NaxError` this feature's forge functions throw carries `stage: "forge"` in its context (`.nax/rules/error-handling.md`). Every read and write goes through the `gh api` / `glab api` REST or GraphQL endpoints with an explicit `--hostname`, never the CLI's implicit repo context.

**Scope** — In: extend src/forge/pr-read.ts created by US-003 with readPrInfo, export it from forge/index.ts, and add pr-read-info.test.ts; use US-003's PrRef/PrInfo and encodeProjectPath. Out: US-003 owns reference resolution and types; US-005 owns trust decisions and current-user lookups; other stories own threads, comments and writes. Metadata only: no checkout, command or production caller is added.

**Interface** — `readPrInfo(ref: PrRef, deps, cwd): Promise<PrInfo>`; deps is the existing ForgeDeps and cwd is the checkout directory passed unchanged to deps.run(argv, { cwd }). Tests build PrRef by hand, import readPrInfo through @/forge and verify explicit host/endpoint argv and mapped values against mocked JSON. Keep existing pr-read.test.ts unchanged while adding the dedicated mapping tests.

userStories.title: Read the current user and classify PR trust
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read the authenticated forge identity and classify PR author trust using metadata only.

**Motivation** — The forge layer can open, view, edit and promote a PR, and post one top-level comment (`packages/nax/src/workflow/promote.ts`). It cannot read review threads or comments, post on a line, reply in a thread, resolve a thread, or tell a fork PR from a trusted one.

**Approach** — `classifyPrTrust(ref: PrRef, info: PrInfo, deps, cwd): Promise<PrTrust>` - never throws. Rules, in order; the first that decides wins:
1. `info.crossRepo` -> untrusted, reason `head branch is not in the base repository`.
2. The author is the current user -> trusted, reason `author is the current user`. The current user comes from `readCurrentUser` (below). When both `info.author.id` and the current user's `id` are known they are compared; otherwise the logins are compared.
3. The author has write access -> trusted, reason `author has write access`. GitHub `gh api --hostname <host> repos/<repo>/collaborators/<login>/permission` -> `.permission` is `admin` or `write` (the legacy field maps `maintain` to `write`). GitLab `glab api --hostname <host> projects/<enc>/members/all/<author.id>` -> `.access_level >= 30`; a lookup that exits non-zero with `404` in its stderr means the author is not a member: rule 4.
4. Otherwise -> untrusted, reason `author has no write access`.
Rule 1 runs first on purpose, so the current user's own PR from a fork is untrusted too (fail closed; B3's `--trust` is the way through). Every result carries `headSha: info.headSha`.
Any non-zero exit or unparseable reply in rules 2-3 -> untrusted with reason `could not read <what>: <stderr, trimmed, first 200 chars>`; a GitLab author with no `id` cannot be looked up and is untrusted the same way.

`readCurrentUser(ref, deps, cwd): Promise<CurrentUser>` - GitHub `gh api --hostname <host> user` -> `{ login: .login, id: .id }`; GitLab `glab api --hostname <host> user` -> `{ login: .username, id: .id }`. A non-zero exit throws `FORGE_USER_READ_FAILED`; an unparseable reply or a missing login throws `FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE`. `classifyPrTrust` catches both and turns them into a `could not read` reason.

Nothing here reads the PR's title, body, diff or comments: trust comes from forge metadata only (§5a), and nothing is cached or stored.

`encodeProjectPath(repo: string): string` - `encodeURIComponent(repo)` (`group/proj` -> `group%2Fproj`), the GitLab project id every GitLab endpoint in this feature uses. Every other value interpolated into an endpoint path (logins, ids) also goes through `encodeURIComponent`, so `dependabot[bot]` stays one segment. Every `NaxError` this feature's forge functions throw carries `stage: "forge"` in its context (`.nax/rules/error-handling.md`).

**Scope** — In: create trust.ts with readCurrentUser/classifyPrTrust, add trust.test.ts and export both functions from @/forge; consume US-003's types and encoding and US-004's PrInfo contract. Out: US-004 owns reading PR details; US-006/007 own discussion reads; US-011 composes ownership detection. Trust enforcement, static review mode and --trust belong to B2/B3; this story returns classification only. A trust result is never cached or stored; rechecking after a push is the caller's job using PrTrust.headSha. GitHub organisation team permissions beyond the collaborator permission endpoint are not read.

**Interface** — `classifyPrTrust(ref: PrRef, info: PrInfo, deps, cwd): Promise<PrTrust>` and `readCurrentUser(ref, deps, cwd): Promise<CurrentUser>` use existing ForgeDeps and a string cwd. PrTrust has trusted, headSha and never-empty ordered reasons; CurrentUser has login and optional numeric id. Tests construct refs/info and drive the real functions through mocked ForgeDeps, including no calls for crossRepo, hostile title/body, identity precedence, encoded logins and failing lookups. No production caller is added.

userStories.title: Read paginated review threads on both forges
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read review threads with stable reply/edit identities and bounded explicit pagination. **Motivation** — The forge layer can open, view, edit and promote a PR, and post one top-level comment (`packages/nax/src/workflow/promote.ts`). It cannot read review threads or comments, post on a line, reply in a thread, resolve a thread, or tell a fork PR from a trusted one. **Approach** — `listReviewThreads(ref, deps, cwd): Promise` - GitHub: GraphQL through `gh api --hostname graphql -f query= -f owner= -f name= -F number=` plus `-f endCursor=` after the first page, where `/` is `ref.repo` split at the first `/`. `Q` selects `repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads(first: 100, after: $endCursor)` with `pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }` and per node `id isResolved isOutdated path line originalLine comments(first: 100) { nodes { databaseId author { login } body createdAt } }`. Loops while `hasNextPage`. A thread maps to `id`, `replyTo = String(comments[0].databaseId)`, `path`, `line = line ?? originalLine` (absent when both are null), `resolved = isResolved`, `outdated = isOutdated`, comments of kind `thread` with `id = String(databaseId)`, `author = author.login` (a deleted author reads as `ghost`), `body`, `createdAt` (the `id` is what `editComment` takes). - GitLab: `glab api --hostname projects//merge_requests//discussions?per_page=100&page=

` for `p = 1, 2, ...` until a page returns fewer than 100 items. Discussions with `individual_note: false` are threads: `id = replyTo = discussion.id`, `path = notes[0].position?.new_path ?? old_path`, `line = notes[0].position?.new_line ?? old_line`, `resolved = notes[0].resolved === true`, `outdated: false`, comments = the non-system notes, kind `thread`, `id = String(note.id)`, `author = note.author.username`, `createdAt = note.created_at`. Both: a page loop stops with `NaxError` `FORGE_PAGINATION_LIMIT` when a 51st page would be needed (GitHub `hasNextPage` still true after page 50, or a full 100-item REST/GitLab page 50), with `MAX_FORGE_PAGES = 50` exported; a non-zero exit throws `FORGE_THREADS_READ_FAILED` (threads) or `FORGE_COMMENTS_READ_FAILED` (comments); an unparseable page throws `FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE`. Items keep the forge's order. Every read and write goes through the `gh api` / `glab api` REST or GraphQL endpoints with an explicit `--hostname`, never the CLI's implicit repo context. Pagination is nax's own loop over explicit `page` numbers or GraphQL cursors, never the CLI's `--paginate` flag, so a mocked `ForgeDeps` sees every page request. Every `NaxError` this feature's forge functions throw carries `stage: "forge"` in its context (`.nax/rules/error-handling.md`). **Scope** — In: create threads.ts with listReviewThreads, MAX_FORGE_PAGES and shared page-loop machinery; export the public reader/constant from @/forge and add threads.test.ts. US-007 reuses this loop and pins shared GitLab discussion paging. Out: US-007 adds top-level comment reads; US-008–010 add writes; US-011 composes own-comment discovery. Review thread comments past the first 100 in one thread are not read. GitLab threads always report outdated: false; detecting outdated GitLab positions is not done. **Interface** — `listReviewThreads(ref, deps, cwd): Promise`, with PrRef and ForgeDeps from the existing forge contracts, and exported `MAX_FORGE_PAGES = 50`. Tests build PrRef by hand, import public symbols through @/forge and assert every requested page against ForgeDeps.run. Preserve forge order; keep thread id, replyTo and comment id distinct on GitHub. Shared helpers must allow US-007 to select its own read-failure code without duplicating the pagination algorithm.

userStories.title: Guard forge writes and post summary comments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Establish shared safe write validation/execution and post top-level PR comments.

**Motivation** — The forge layer can open, view, edit and promote a PR, and post one top-level comment (`packages/nax/src/workflow/promote.ts`). It cannot read review threads or comments, post on a line, reply in a thread, resolve a thread, or tell a fork PR from a trusted one.

**Approach** — Every string field goes on the argv as `-f key=value` (raw field), never `-F`: `gh`/`glab` read `-F key=@path` as a file, so a body or path starting with `@` would post a local file. Integers use `-F`.

`glab api` does not nest bracketed field names: `-f position[new_line]=5` is sent as the flat JSON key `"position[new_line]"`, which GitLab does not read as a position (checked with glab 1.100.0 against a stub server, 2026-10-20). So the GitLab inline comment puts its `position` in the endpoint's query string, built with `URLSearchParams` (GitLab merges query and body params), and sends only `-f body=` as a field. `--form` is never used: it uploads any value starting with `@` as a file.

| Function | GitHub argv (after `gh api --hostname <host>`) | GitLab argv (after `glab api --hostname <host>`) | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `postPrComment(ref, body)` | `-X POST repos/<repo>/issues/<n>/comments -f body=` | `-X POST projects/<enc>/merge_requests/<n>/notes -f body=` | `{ id, url? }` |

Checks before any call: an empty or whitespace-only body throws `FORGE_COMMENT_EMPTY`; a body longer than `MAX_FORGE_COMMENT_CHARS = 65_536` throws `FORGE_COMMENT_TOO_LONG`; a GitLab inline comment without `diffRefs` throws `FORGE_DIFF_REFS_REQUIRED`; editing a GitHub comment of kind `review` throws `FORGE_EDIT_UNSUPPORTED`; an inline `line` that is not a positive integer, or an empty `path`, throws `FORGE_COMMENT_TARGET_INVALID`; an id interpolated into a URL path that fails its pattern throws `FORGE_ID_INVALID`: GitHub `replyTo` and comment `id` must be all digits, a GitLab discussion id (`replyTo`, thread `id`) must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, and a GitLab note `id` must be all digits. B2 may pass ids that came from agent output, so `d1/../x` must never reach a path. The body length is `body.length` (UTF-16 code units, which never undercounts characters). A non-zero exit throws `FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED` with `stage: "forge"`, `forge`, `exitCode` and the trimmed stderr in the context. Writes are never retried: a retried POST can post twice. All of this lives in two shared helpers in `forge/comments.ts`: `assertCommentBody(body)` (the empty and length checks) and `runForgeWrite(ref, argv, deps, cwd)` (one `deps.run`, the non-zero-exit error, JSON reply parsing), which every write function goes through.

Every `NaxError` this feature's forge functions throw carries `stage: "forge"` in its context (`.nax/rules/error-handling.md`).

**Scope** — In: create comments.ts with MAX_FORGE_COMMENT_CHARS, assertCommentBody, runForgeWrite and postPrComment; export public function/constant from @/forge; add comments.test.ts. The shared helpers remain available within comments.ts for later extensions. Out: US-009 adds inline position/target validation and posting; US-010 adds reply/resolve/edit and their id guards. The quoted write-family rules constrain those extensions, not extra capabilities to implement here. Rendering/escaping agent text belongs to B2; this layer posts its given body. Rate-limit back-off and retrying a failed write are not done; a retried POST can post twice.

**Interface** — `postPrComment(ref, body)` returns PostedComment (`{ id, url? }`), using PrRef, body string, injected ForgeDeps and cwd as the other forge operations do. `assertCommentBody(body)` checks empty/whitespace and maximum UTF-16 length; `runForgeWrite(ref, argv, deps, cwd)` executes exactly once and parses the JSON response, throwing FORGE_RESPONSE_UNPARSEABLE for non-JSON success output. Tests import public symbols through @/forge, construct refs by hand and assert raw -f bodies (especially @/etc/passwd), exact host/method/endpoint argv, response ids and structured failure context. No production caller or live write is added.

**Motivation** — The forge layer can open, view, edit and promote a PR, and post one top-level comment (`packages/nax/src/workflow/promote.ts`). It cannot read review threads or comments, post on a line, reply in a thread, resolve a thread, or tell a fork PR from a trusted one.

Checks before any call: an empty or whitespace-only body throws `FORGE_COMMENT_EMPTY`; a body longer than `MAX_FORGE_COMMENT_CHARS = 65_536` throws `FORGE_COMMENT_TOO_LONG`; editing a GitHub comment of kind `review` throws `FORGE_EDIT_UNSUPPORTED`; an id interpolated into a URL path that fails its pattern throws `FORGE_ID_INVALID`: GitHub `replyTo` and comment `id` must be all digits, a GitLab discussion id (`replyTo`, thread `id`) must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, and a GitLab note `id` must be all digits. B2 may pass ids that came from agent output, so `d1/../x` must never reach a path. The body length is `body.length` (UTF-16 code units, which never undercounts characters). A non-zero exit throws `FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED` with `stage: "forge"`, `forge`, `exitCode` and the trimmed stderr in the context. Writes are never retried: a retried POST can post twice.

All of this lives in two shared helpers in `forge/comments.ts`: `assertCommentBody(body)` (the empty and length checks) and `runForgeWrite(ref, argv, deps, cwd)` (one `deps.run`, the non-zero-exit error, JSON reply parsing), which every write function goes through. Every other value interpolated into an endpoint path (logins, ids) also goes through `encodeURIComponent`, so `dependabot[bot]` stays one segment. userStories.title: Mark nax bot comments and find the current user's own comments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the stable bot marker and discover only marked comments authored by the authenticated user.

**Motivation** — The step graph master plan (`nax-step-graph-and-bot-master-plan.md`, rulings R1-R11) builds `nax bot review` and `nax bot fix`, which QA any PR: read every comment, check each one, fix or answer it.

**Approach** — Marker (`forge/marker.ts`):
- `NAX_BOT_HEADER = "**nax bot**"`.
- `withNaxBotMarker(body: string, key: string): string` returns `` `${NAX_BOT_HEADER}\n\n${body}\n\n<!-- nax-bot:v1 key=${key} -->` ``. `key` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$`, else `NaxError` `FORGE_MARKER_KEY_INVALID` (so a key can never close the HTML comment early).
- `parseNaxBotMarker(body: string): { key: string } | null` - the key of the last `<!-- nax-bot:v1 key=<key> -->` in the body whose key matches the same pattern, else null.
- `findOwnComments(ref, deps, cwd): Promise<OwnComment[]>` - `readCurrentUser`, then `listReviewThreads`, then `listPrComments`; every comment whose body parses to a marker **and whose author is the current user's login**, with the thread's `id` as `threadId` for thread comments. Thread comments come first, in thread order. Anyone can paste a marker into a comment; only the author check makes it nax bot's own (R7: nax bot posts as the user's login). A failure of any of the three reads propagates.

`forge/index.ts` (the barrel; `check:alias-internals` forbids reaching past it) exports every function, constant and type above. Every `NaxError` this feature's forge functions throw carries `stage: "forge"` in its context (`.nax/rules/error-handling.md`).

**Scope** — In: create marker.ts and marker.test.ts; export NAX_BOT_HEADER/withNaxBotMarker/parseNaxBotMarker/findOwnComments from @/forge. findOwnComments calls US-005's readCurrentUser and US-006/US-007's listReviewThreads/listPrComments; its ACs drive it with a mocked ForgeDeps that answers all three endpoints and assert each was read. Out: US-005 owns identity/trust lookup; US-006/007 own readers; US-008–010 own posting/editing. This story does not post, escape/render agent content, add a CLI caller or decide thread-resolution policy.

**Interface** — `withNaxBotMarker(body: string, key: string): string`; `parseNaxBotMarker(body: string): { key: string } | null`; `findOwnComments(ref, deps, cwd): Promise<OwnComment[]>`; constant `NAX_BOT_HEADER = "**nax bot**"`. OwnComment is `{ readonly comment: PrComment; readonly threadId?: string; readonly key: string }` from US-003. Compose the real upstream functions using the provided ForgeDeps rather than replacing them with disconnected stubs. Tests import all new public symbols through @/forge, exercise the read sequence and ordering with endpoint-driven fakes, reject forged ownership and propagate reader failures. No live forge test or production caller is added.

Trust: classifyPrTrust is security-sensitive access classification, so US-005 uses strict three-session-tdd. Reject cross-repo before making any lookup, including a user's own fork PR. Compare ids if both exist, otherwise logins; mismatching ids cannot be rescued by equal names. Permission endpoints alone decide author write access; title/body/diff/comments are never consulted and no trust is cached. GitLab missing author id, malformed/nonzero current-user/permission replies and thrown dependency errors fail closed with bounded reasons; only GitLab membership 404 means ordinary no write access. Every result includes the classified headSha for caller-controlled rechecks after pushes.

Threads/comments: create threads.ts in US-006 and extend it in US-007. GitHub GraphQL uses cursor variables and 100 threads/page with the first 100 comments per thread; REST uses explicit per_page=100&page=N. Shared loops preserve forge order and enforce the 50-page cap before a 51st request, including a full final REST page even if the next page could be empty. Do not use --paginate. GitHub thread node id is for resolving, first comment database id is for replying, and each comment database id is for editing. Preserve these distinct identities and null line/originalLine fallback; deleted GitHub authors become ghost. GitLab discussions are split by individual_note and system notes are filtered; first-note position/resolved metadata is still the mapping source. Root comments are GitHub issue comments followed by nonempty review bodies, or GitLab individual-note discussions. Validate JSON/page shape rather than allowing incidental TypeErrors; request failure codes differ for threads and top-level comments.

Writes/security: create comments.ts/helpers in US-008, extend in US-009 and US-010, and keep all three stories on strict three-session-tdd because raw-field handling and endpoint-id validation protect file disclosure/path traversal boundaries. Every body-bearing operation uses assertCommentBody; every write, including resolve, uses one runForgeWrite call, parses JSON and never retries. Resolve has no body, so do not fabricate an empty body merely to call the body validator. Strings including body/path/SHA/GraphQL fields use -f, integer line/number use -F; never --form. The literal @ prefix must remain text, not become a file read. GitLab inline position belongs in URLSearchParams in the endpoint, not bracketed CLI fields. IDs interpolated into URL paths are validated before the only CLI call and then encoded. GitHub GraphQL thread node ids are raw variables, not numeric URL ids. NaxError write contexts contain stage, forge, exitCode and trimmed stderr. Shared-file growth is a risk: keep helpers short and follow the existing file-size rules without moving capabilities out of the specified modules gratuitously.

Markers/ownership: US-011 depends on trust and both readers and uses strict three-session-tdd because ownership filtering is an authorization boundary. Validate keys against the bounded safe alphabet, parse the last valid marker, and identify own comments only through current-user login plus marker, not marker/header alone. findOwnComments must call the real current-user, thread and top-level readers using the supplied ForgeDeps, in that order; endpoint-driven mocks prove all seams and failure propagation. Thread results precede top-level results and retain threadId only where appropriate.

outOfScope: The `nax bot review` and `nax bot fix` commands, their graphs, CLI wiring and command name (Q2) are B2 and B3; this feature adds no CLI command and no production caller of `buildPrStepContext` or of any new forge function.
Deciding which config a PR is reviewed under (loading config, rules, plugins and hooks from the base branch, master plan §5a) is B2; `buildPrStepContext` takes the config it is given.
The static review mode for untrusted PRs (no Bash, no gates, no network) is B2, and `--trust` with sandboxed gates is B3; `classifyPrTrust` only returns the classification.

Allowing `n/a` in the branch review verdict's `spec` field, and judging intent from the PR description and linked issues (R9), are B2; the verdict schema and `workflowBranchReviewOp` do not change here.
Checking out the PR head into a throwaway worktree, and persisting bot run state under the nax output dir, are B2.
Rendering and escaping comment text from agent output, and any length cap stricter than the forge limit, are B2; the forge write functions post the body they are given.
Whether `nax bot fix` resolves threads (Q1) is B3; `resolveThread` is only the capability.
The story-loop steps keep `StepContext`; giving them a narrow context is not needed by the bot and is not done here.
The publish and final-gate steps (`publish`, `finalize.ts`) keep `FeatureContext`; the bot posts through the new forge functions instead.
`FeatureContext`, `buildFeatureContext`, `buildFeatureEnv` and `featureModelFor` do not change.
A repo whose `origin` is a fork of the PR's base repo resolves to the fork's slug; detecting the upstream remote is not done.
Review thread comments past the first 100 in one thread are not read (GitHub GraphQL `comments(first: 100)`).
GitLab threads always report `outdated: false`; detecting outdated GitLab positions is not done.

Multi-line inline comments (`start_line`, GitLab line ranges) are not supported; an inline comment targets one new-side line, and a GitLab comment on an unchanged context line (which needs `old_line`) is not supported.
Forge hosts with a port (`git.corp:8443`) are not supported: `remoteHost` drops the port and `glab api --hostname` rejects `host:port`.
US-005 only: a trust result is never cached or stored; each call reads the forge again (§5a forbids a standing setting). Re-checking trust after a push is the caller's job, using `PrTrust.headSha`.
US-005 only: GitHub organisation team permissions beyond the collaborator permission endpoint are not read.
US-008 only: rate-limit back-off and retrying a failed write are not done; a retried POST can post twice.
Pipeline mode is frozen: no pipeline-only code is touched.
One live check of the forge functions against a throwaway PR is a manual step after merge, with the user's go; no test posts to a real forge.
No release is part of this feature.
